bundle.author: jagoda
bundle.title: Make the Bifrost gateway claim its first admin, and keep it
bundle.body:
`bifrost.workbench.goodparty.org` has been asking for the setup token on every navigation because **no admin account has ever existed**. This makes the claim work and makes it stick. It is a fix, not a feature: the deployed gateway is running Bifrost's built-in defaults.

Plan: docs/bifrost-gateway.md
Step: 11
Step: 10

### Why the claim has been failing (`31cdd0a`, step 11)

The claim container was logging this on every task start:

```
2026-10-26T16:17:05Z warn log_retention_days must be at least 1
2026-10-26T16:17:05Z warn request completed    PUT /api/config 400
```

`GET /api/config` returns `client_config.log_retention_days: 0` for a store that has never saved a retention, and `PUT /api/config` refuses anything below 1 (`handlers/config.go:573` at the pinned tag). The claim deliberately echoes the server's own view back so it cannot drop settings the store holds, so every fresh store got a guaranteed 400 — and, because the response body was discarded, a bare status code was the only trace.

The first-admin validation (`config.go:443-470`) runs *before* that check, so the stored admin password and setup token are both valid; no `fill-secrets.sh --force` is needed. The script now raises that one field to the smallest value the write path accepts, leaves every other value untouched, and prints the server's `error` text on a rejection. `config.json`'s 90 days stays authoritative where it belongs.

`README.md`'s documented check — `curl .../api/session/is-auth-enabled` "from anywhere" — could never have worked: Bifrost whitelists it, but `/api/*` is routed to oauth2-proxy, so it is a 302 to Google. Corrected rather than left as a trap.

### Why the account also had to stop disappearing (`3be6c8b`, step 10)

With no `config_store`, Bifrost creates a SQLite file inside the container, so the account died with every task replacement — and the repo's whole `governance` block, `enforce_auth_on_inference` and `disable_content_logging` were inert, because `BIFROST_CONFIG` was never injected. The log said so plainly: `config file not found at path: /app/data/config.json, initializing with default values`.

`config.json` is now stored in the SSM parameter `bifrost/config`, injected as `BIFROST_CONFIG`, and written to `/app/data/config.json` by the container entry point using upstream's own documented ECS shape (write, then `exec /app/docker-entrypoint.sh /app/main`, so PID 1, the app-dir checks and signal handling stay the image's). A task with no config exits instead of booting on defaults. `config_store` and `logs_store` are both Postgres against item 7's instance, with the connection values coming from `rds.ts` rather than a connection string spelled a second time in JSON.

### The one deliberate deviation from the plan

The plan says SSM **SecureString**; this uses **String**. The file holds no secret by construction — every credential in it is an `env.NAME` reference, which `config.test.ts` enforces — so encryption would buy nothing, while a `SecureString` would make the ECS agent hold `kms:Decrypt` on the account's `aws/ssm` key, which cannot be scoped without a wildcard or a deploy-time key lookup that the preview role would then need. Argued in the constant's comment; say so if you want the SecureString and a CMK instead, and it is a small follow-up.

### What lands before its dependency

`client.enforce_auth_on_inference: true` becomes effective with this apply and item 14's virtual keys do not exist yet, so inference refuses everything until they do. That is the plan's phase A order ("inference succeeds with a virtual key and fails without one") and nothing depends on the gateway yet, but the two items want to land close together — flagging it rather than quietly seeding keys.

First boot after the apply runs ~50 store migrations against an empty RDS inside the 30s start period, and the admin account is provisioned from the file at boot, which makes the claim container a no-op from then on.

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes gateway boot path, auth enforcement, and persistence; mis-deploy or missing item 14 virtual keys can block all inference until keys exist.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a live Bifrost gateway that never claimed an admin and lost state on every deploy by wiring **phase 2 item 10** and patching the **item 11** bootstrap path.
> 
> **Config delivery and durability.** `config.json` now declares Postgres `config_store` and `logs_store` (RDS via `PG_*` env refs). Pulumi stores the reviewed file in SSM `bifrost/config` as a plain **String**, injects `BIFROST_CONFIG`, and overrides the gateway entrypoint to write `/app/data/config.json` then `exec` upstream’s entrypoint—tasks without config **exit** instead of SQLite defaults. The execution role gains scoped `ssm:GetParameters` on that parameter.
> 
> **Bootstrap claim fix.** `bootstrap.sh` raises `client_config.log_retention_days` to **1** when the store returns **0** (GET/PUT validation mismatch that caused every first `PUT /api/config` to 400), preserves existing retention when already set, and logs the server’s `error` body on failure.
> 
> **Tests and docs.** `config.test.ts`, `ecs.test.ts`, and `bootstrap.test.ts` lock Postgres store shape, env injection, SSM wiring, and bootstrap behavior; README notes deploy ordering (`enforce_auth_on_inference` before item 14 virtual keys) and that public `curl` to `is-auth-enabled` hits oauth2-proxy, not Bifrost.

priorFindings.body: The SSM parameter name `bifrost/config` contains a `/` but does not start with one. SSM expects a hierarchical name to be fully qualified, with a leading slash; my understanding is that `PutParameter` rejects `bifrost/config` with a ValidationException ("Parameter name must be a fully qualified name"). If so, `pulumi up` fails when it tries to create `bifrostConfigParameter`, and the task definition and execution role that depend on its ARN never deploy. The only other `aws.ssm.Parameter` in this repo, `GROUP_SYNC_PARAMETER_NAME` in `deploy-infrastructure/group-sync-lambda.ts`, uses `/identity-group-sync/pairs`. Use `/bifrost/config` instead; the ARN is still `...:parameter/bifrost/config`. The equality assertion in `ecs.test.ts` that pins the name to `"bifrost/config"` needs the same change. Falsification check: this finding is wrong if SSM accepts a name containing `/` without a leading slash. I could not confirm that against the AWS API from the checkout, and the one precedent in the repo uses the leading slash.

findings.body:
**Editing `config.json` will not change the running gateway.** The task definition points at the parameter only by its ARN (`valueFrom: configParameterArn`, line 959), and the ARN stays the same when the value changes. When a `config.json` edit merges, `pulumi up` updates the SSM parameter. It does not register a new task-definition revision or replace any task.

ECS reads `secrets` values only when a task starts, so running tasks keep the old config until something unrelated replaces them. Two examples: removing a model from the allowlist, or adding item 14's virtual keys. The Pulumi diff shows either one as applied while the live gateway still runs the previous file.

That breaks two things this PR relies on:
- the comment just above (line 734), which says "a configuration change is a PR that registers a new task-definition revision";
- `source_of_truth: "config.json"`.

**Fix:** put a hash of the config's content into the container definition, so the task definition changes whenever the file does. For example, add a plain env entry `BIFROST_CONFIG_SHA256` set to the sha256 of `readBifrostConfig()`. Alternatively, inject the value directly.

**Falsification check:** I found no `forceNewDeployment`, content hash or trigger in `deploy-workbench/ecs.ts`, and the container definition depends only on `configParameter.arn`. If some other mechanism in the service or task definition already changes with the file's content, this finding is wrong.

output.summary:
This PR does what its description says, with one gap, flagged inline. `config.json` gets Postgres `config_store`/`logs_store` that read their connection settings from `env.PG_*` values. `ecs.ts` stores the file in a plain-String SSM parameter (`/bifrost/config`), injects it as `BIFROST_CONFIG` with a scoped `ssm:GetParameters` grant, and replaces the gateway's entry point so the config is written to `/app/data/config.json` before handing off to upstream's entrypoint. `bootstrap.sh` raises a zero `log_retention_days` to 1 and prints the server's error text when the claim is rejected.

The scout raised five leads; deep reviewers ruled out four and confirmed one:
- **Ruled out, wiring:** every `env.` name in the config is supplied to the gateway container, the `pulumi.all` order matches its destructuring, the `rds.ts` exports exist, and the test text-matching fragments are present in the source.
- **Ruled out, bootstrap shell:** the Alpine/busybox image supports the new `local` and `head -c` use, and the jq retention logic is correct for null, 0 and 90.
- **Ruled out, file permissions:** nothing in the repo suggests the `umask 077` write breaks under the upstream entrypoint.
- **Ruled out, size:** the file is about 2.4 KB, under the 4 KB Standard-tier cap.
- **Confirmed:** a later `config.json` change will not restart tasks, because the task definition depends only on the parameter's ARN.

The prior finding about the SSM name's missing leading slash is fixed: the name is now `/bifrost/config`, and a test pins it.

Two things a human should confirm, since they couldn't be checked from the repo:
- Upstream's image keeps `/app/data` writable and runs as the same user after `exec`.
- First boot finishes the store migrations against the empty RDS within the health-check start period.

Also note that `enforce_auth_on_inference` takes effect with this apply, before item 14's virtual keys exist.
